summary: FM (Frequency Modulation) synthesis creates complex harmonic content by using one oscillator to modulate the frequency of another. Developed by John Chowning at Stanford in the 1960s, it powers classic synthesizers like the Yamaha DX7.

concepts.name: Carrier
concepts.description: The oscillator that produces the audible output

concepts.name: Modulator
concepts.description: The oscillator that modulates the carrier's frequency

concepts.name: Aliasing
concepts.description: High modulation indices can cause aliasing. Use oversampling or limit modulation.

concepts.name: CPU Cost
concepts.description: FM is efficient, but many operators add up. Start simple.

concepts.name: Tuning
concepts.description: Non-integer ratios can sound out of tune. Use harmonic ratios for melodic sounds.

concepts.name: Envelopes
concepts.description: FM needs envelope control on modulators too, not just carriers.

code_blocks.code:
// Algorithm: Modulator → Carrier
modulatorRatio = 14.0f;      // Slightly detuned from carrier
modulationIndex = 1.5f;      // Moderate brightness
carrierEnv.setAttack(1);     // Instant
carrierEnv.setDecay(100);    // Medium decay
modulatorEnv.setDecay(200);  // Longer than carrier

// Non-integer ratio for inharmonic spectrum
modulatorRatio = 1.4f;       // Creates metallic character
modulationIndex = 3.0f;     // Bright
modulatorEnv.setDecay(2000); // Long decay
carrierEnv.setDecay(3000);   // Very long
modulatorEnv.setSustain(0);  // No sustain
carrierEnv.setSustain(0);    // Pure decay

Mod1 → Carrier 1 → Output
Mod2 → Carrier 2 → Output
    ↘ Carrier 3 → Output

title: FM Synthesis Sound Design
description: Frequency modulation synthesis techniques for complex harmonic sounds
